title: Agents
intro: RuntimeAgent owns scheduling, asynchronous context and the global symbol registry and may own multiple realms. Host-created agents can run independently and share narrow cluster services. The section remains Incomplete because the agent-wide asynchronous module evaluation order counter is not implemented.

entries.feature: Opaque identity for host-created runtime agents
entries.notes: Distinct RuntimeAgent instances supply stable opaque ownership identities for realms, schedulers, symbol registries, shared-memory access and Atomics waiters. This is an internal host ownership model, not a public JavaScript agent or worker API.

entries.feature: AgentCanSuspend behavior in host event loop
entries.notes: The host implements blocking Atomics.wait, asynchronous waits, independent per-agent event-loop scheduling and cooperative shutdown. Agents can notify waiters in the same cluster. A configurable ECMAScript agent suspension-policy slot is not modeled.

Native ESM already supports top-level await, promise-backed dependency completion and cached evaluation failures. Require.EsModuleEvaluation uses module-local pending-dependency counts, not the agent-wide monotonic asynchronous evaluation order counter specified here. That operation and full general asynchronous cyclic-module ordering remain unimplemented; the referenced tests cover supported async graphs, not this missing counter.
